about.title: A deeper look
about.body:
I'm a developer, but my path to code led through mathematics, biophysics, laboratories and factory floors. That's probably why I most enjoy work where you need to understand how the pieces fit together... from data and logic all the way to the person who ends up using it.

When I'm not building something or taking it apart in my head, I'm probably reading, somewhere in the hills, moving, or exploring something I knew almost nothing about yesterday. I like useful things, plain human decency, and solutions that don't have to be more complicated than necessary.

I'm also a coffee person who loves good food and music.

bitstream.label: Bit Stream
bitstream.desc: Tilt the bit stream: send 1s to the servers (SRV) and 0s to spam. Right bin +2 points, wrong bin −1. Bits fall in runs of 3–7 identical values. Watch what's coming. And mind the codes: 200 OK enables auto-routing for a few seconds, 500 resets your score, and 404 ends the run on the spot.
bitstream.controls: Controls: arrow keys ← → (or A/D). Start: space or click. Switch game speed on the title screen with 1/2/3 or by tapping. Catch 200, dodge 500 and 404.

surprisal.label: Surprisal
surprisal.desc: You are a text cursor running through a sentence generated token by token by a language model, for real: logits → temperature → softmax → sampling. Every obstacle is one sampled token: the less likely it was, the bigger it is. Your score is bits of surprise (surprisal), so risk equals reward. Temperature gates, a top-p shield, a greedy star and context windows change how the model picks, exactly like the real thing.
surprisal.controls: Controls: space / ↑ / tap = jump, ↓ or S = duck under hallucinations. Run through a HOT/COLD gate on the ground, or jump over it. P/Esc = pause, R = restart.

ticker.hot: T = 1.6 → flatter distribution: rare tokens more likely, more bits
ticker.cold: T = 0.5 → sharper distribution: playing it safe, fewer bits
ticker.rare: "{word}" had only {pct}% → surprisal {bits} bits → huge obstacle!
ticker.shield: top-p 0.9: distribution tail cut off, rare tokens won't drop now
ticker.greedy: greedy: always the most likely token, easy, but almost no bits
ticker.ctx: context full → more confident predictions → bits ×2
ticker.hallu: hallucination! a nonsense token, duck under it (↓)

results.inspect: Click a token in the sentence to see how the model picked it.
results.whatBody: Every obstacle was one generated token. The model picked from real probabilities (softmax over logits, shaped by temperature). Rare tokens carried more bits of surprise (surprisal), which is why they were bigger. Run perplexity = 2^(average surprisal).

garbage.label: Garbage Collector
garbage.desc: Classic snake dressed up as a memory manager: you are the pointer, eating memory leaks. Every block you swallow frees kilobytes, but your heap grows with it. Every 8 leaks a GC cycle runs: the heap gets compacted (the snake shrinks), but the system speeds up. And from the second cycle on, dangling pointers ✗ appear in memory, don't touch those.
garbage.controls: Controls: arrow keys or WASD, swipe on mobile. Start: spacebar or tap. Blinking blocks are fragmented leaks: they vanish quickly but pay triple. Don't hit the walls, yourself, or the ✗.
